1: Kṛṣṇa, you praise the renunciation of actions, and then again you praise yoga. Tell me for certain which one of the two is better.
2: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good. But of the two, the yoga of action is better than the renunciation of action.
3: A person who neither hates nor longs should be known as a constant renouncer. For one who is free from the pairs of opposites, mighty-armed one, is easily released from bondage.
4: It is the childish, not the learned, who say that sāṅkhya and yoga are separate. One who is rightly established in even one of them finds the fruit of both.
5: The place reached by the followers of sāṅkhya is reached by the followers of yoga too. Whoever sees sāṅkhya and yoga as one is the one who sees.
6: But renunciation, mighty-armed one, is hard to reach without yoga. The sage who is yoked by yoga reaches brahman before long.
7: One who is yoked by yoga, whose self is purified, who has conquered the self and conquered the senses, and whose self has become the self of all beings, is not stained even while acting.
8: While seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping and breathing, one who is yoked and knows the truth should think: I do nothing at all.
9: While talking, letting go, grasping, and even opening and closing the eyes, such a person holds to this: the senses are moving among the objects of the senses.
10: One who acts after placing actions in brahman and giving up attachment is not stained by evil, just as a lotus leaf is not stained by water.
11: Yogīs act with the body, with the mind, with the buddhi, and even with the senses alone. They give up attachment and act to purify the self.
12: One who is yoked gives up the fruit of action and attains final peace. One who is not yoked is attached to the fruit through the working of desire, and is bound.
13: Having renounced all actions with the mind, the embodied one sits happily and in control in the city of nine gates, neither acting at all nor causing action.
14: The lord creates neither the world's doership, nor its actions, nor the link between an action and its fruit. It is one's own nature that is at work.
15: The all-pervading one does not take on anyone's evil, nor anyone's good deeds either. Knowledge is covered by ignorance, and that is why creatures are deluded.
16: But for those whose ignorance has been destroyed by knowledge of the self, that knowledge, like the sun, lights up that which is supreme.
17: Those whose buddhi rests in that, whose self is that, whose foundation is that and whose highest goal is that, go where there is no return, their stains shaken off by knowledge.
18: The learned see the same in a brāhmaṇa rich in learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, and even in a dog and in one who cooks dogs.
19: Those whose mind stands in sameness have conquered creation right here. For brahman is flawless and the same, and so they stand in brahman.
20: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant, nor shudder on getting what is unpleasant. With a steady buddhi and free of delusion, the knower of brahman stands in brahman.
21: One whose self is not attached to outer contacts finds the happiness that is in the self. With the self yoked by the yoga of brahman, such a person attains a happiness that does not decay.
22: For the enjoyments born of contact are nothing but wombs of pain. They have a beginning and an end, son of Kuntī, and the wise one does not delight in them.
23: One who is able, right here, before being released from the body, to withstand the rush that arises from desire and anger is yoked, and is a happy person.
24: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and whose light too is within alone: that yogī, having become brahman, reaches the nirvāṇa of brahman.
25: The seers attain the nirvāṇa of brahman: those whose stains are worn away, whose doubts are cut through, whose self is restrained, and who delight in the good of all beings.
26: For the strivers who are free from desire and anger, whose thought is restrained and who have known the self, the nirvāṇa of brahman lies on every side.
27: The sage shuts outer contacts out, fixes the gaze right between the eyebrows, and makes the in-breath and the out-breath even as they move within the nose.
28: With senses, mind and buddhi restrained, with release as the highest goal, and with wish, fear and anger gone, the sage who is always so is free indeed.
29: Knowing me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all the worlds and the friend of all beings, one comes to peace.
